blurb.text: A Piedmont appellation limited to the commune of Strevi, for wine made only from Moscato Bianco.

sources.name: Candiago et al. 2022, A geospatial inventory of regulatory information for wine protected designations of origin in Europe, Scientific Data (product specifications as of 2021)
Fick and Hijmans 2017, WorldClim 2.1 monthly averages for 1970 to 2000, 2.5 minute grid (about 4.5 km)
Beck et al. 2023, High-resolution (1 km) Koppen-Geiger maps, Scientific Data (1991 to 2020)
Winkler, Cook, Kliewer and Lider 1974, General Viticulture, University of California Press (heat summation regions)
Jones 2010, Climate, grapes, and wine: structure and suitability in a variable and changing climate, VIII International Terroir Congress (which grapes suit which growing season temperatures)
ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0, 1 km aggregates, 30 to 60 cm depth (CC BY 4.0)
USDA NRCS Soil Survey Manual, Agriculture Handbook 18 (texture classes and pH classes)
AWS Terrain Tiles (Terrarium), from SRTM, GMTED2010, ETOPO1 and national elevation models
Wikipedia, Lapse rate (6.5 °C cooler per 1,000 m, the standard atmosphere)
Macrostrat geologic map, the most detailed map unit at each point (CC BY 4.0)
Wikipedia, List of vineyard soil types (revision of 26 November 2025, after Stevenson, Sotheby's Wine Encyclopedia)
SommSelect, A Quick and Dirty Guide to Wine Soils
WSET Level 4 Diploma in Wines, Specification, Issue 1 (2019), the principal regions of Units D3, D4 and D5
